title: mTLS tested with a real peer (both halves), and an interop-day test plan
description: Promised to Rohan Mahy and Konrad Kohbrok in Mark's email of 2026-11-18 (IETF notes/2026-11-18-mimid-interop-answers-sent.md). Before the interop day; Mark offered to do it with Rohan and Konrad. Both halves exist (PKIX inbound mimid-75nk.5, outbound client identity; DANE mimid-75nk.6) but were never deployed or tested with a peer. Write the test plan (which peer, CA or DANE records, which mechanisms, expected results) and run it on the January/December host (mimid-1wgh.46.20.1).
notes:
2026-11-22: THE REAL-PEER HALF IS NOW TESTED, against our own instance
of Haven's mimi-hubd at 34eae7e. Mark authorized running our own Haven
instances, which is what made this possible without Jason's hub.

WHY THE EXISTING HARNESS DID NOT ALREADY COVER IT. tools/interop/haven/
live/up.sh line 14 has SOCAT hold the client certificate and forward to
hubd. So the previous live runs proved that mimi-hubd accepts a PROXY's
certificate, not that it accepts MIMID's. The driver called
PeerClient::new, which uses PeerTlsConfig::default() and presents
nothing. That is exactly the gap this bead names.

WHAT CHANGED: the driver now takes MIMID_CLIENT_CERT, MIMID_CLIENT_KEY
and MIMID_PEER_ROOTS and builds its PeerClient with
PeerClient::with_tls, so mimid presents its own client certificate.
Without the variables it behaves as before, so the socat path still
works.

THE RESULT, driver pointed directly at hubd on localhost:8443, no socat
in the path:

  A. mimid WITHOUT its own certificate
       received fatal alert: CertificateRequired
     i.e. hubd refuses the handshake.

  B. mimid WITH [peer_tls.identity]
       STEP 7a identifierQuery handle bob: 200
       STEP 7b identifierQuery handle nobody: 200
       STEP 8 reportAbuse: 200 (body 0 bytes)
       STEP 6f updateConsent carrying request: 422 (the driver expects
         this; mimid accepts only 202)
     i.e. TLS completes with mimid's own certificate and real protocol
     operations run over it.

The A/B pair is the point: same driver, same target, same CA, differing
only by whether mimid presents a certificate. So mimid's outbound client
identity is accepted by a NON-MIMID implementation, which is what had
never been shown. Previously: two mimid binaries on loopback
(mtls_binaries.rs), or socat holding the certificate.

NO CONFORMANCE CLAIM. Per AGENTS.md this is not a claim of conformance
to protocol-07 §4.1's mutually authenticated TLS; it is one tested
direction against one other implementation, using a throwaway CA in a
namespace. Claiming conformance needs Mark's OK.

STATE OF THE THREE REMAINING ITEMS:
- real-peer test: DONE as above, for the outbound direction with PKIX.
  The inbound direction against a non-mimid peer still needs a peer that
  presents one to us, which on the interop day means Haven doing so.
- reviewcommit.com DNSSEC-signed: ANSWERED, it is (DS at the parent, ad
  flag, RRSIG on the key record).
- DANE through real DNSSEC: still open. No TLSA is published at
  _mimi._client.mimi.reviewcommit.com.
